avgSkip().src: The series to average. Bars where it is absent are passed over, and the mean divides by the number of bars that had a value.
avgSkip().len: How many bars the window covers, this bar included. A whole number of 1 or more.

barsSince().cond: The condition to count from. The count is `0` on a bar where it is true, and a bar where it is absent counts as a bar where it was not true.

change().src: The series whose move is measured, such as `close`.
change().len: How many bars back to compare with, so the result is `src - src[len]`. A whole number of 1 or more. Leave it out to compare with the previous bar.

correlation().a: The first of the two series to compare, such as a stock's `close`.
correlation().b: The second series to compare. Swapping `a` and `b` gives the same result.
correlation().len: How many bars the window covers, this bar included. A whole number of 1 or more.

count().cond: The condition to count. A bar where it is absent counts as not true rather than making the result absent.
count().len: How many bars the window covers, this bar included. A whole number of 1 or more.

countPresent().src: The series to check. A bar counts when its value is present.
countPresent().len: How many bars the window covers, this bar included. A whole number of 1 or more.

covariance().a: The first of the two series.
covariance().b: The second series. Swapping `a` and `b` gives the same result.
covariance().len: How many bars the window covers, this bar included. A whole number of 1 or more.

cross().a: The first of the two values, a series such as a fast average or a fixed number.
cross().b: The second value. A crossing in either direction counts, so the order of `a` and `b` does not matter.

crossDown().a: The value that moves: the result is true on the bar it goes below `b`, having been at or above `b` on the previous bar.
crossDown().b: The value `a` crosses, a series such as a slow average or a fixed number such as `70`.

crossUp().a: The value that moves: the result is true on the bar it goes above `b`, having been at or below `b` on the previous bar.
crossUp().b: The value `a` crosses, a series such as a slow average or a fixed number such as `30`.

cum().src: The series to add up from the first bar. An absent bar gives an absent result on that bar and leaves the total where it was.

falling().src: The series to test, such as an average or an oscillator.
falling().len: How many consecutive one bar changes must all be below zero. A whole number of 1 or more; an unchanged bar breaks the run.

highest().src: The series to search, usually `high` or `close`.
highest().len: How many bars the window covers, this bar included. A whole number of 1 or more.

highestBars().len: How many bars the window covers, this bar included. A whole number of 1 or more.

history().src: The value to read from an earlier bar: a series, an expression such as `close - open`, or an array.
history().n: How many bars back to read. A whole number of 1 or more; `0` stops the script with `OS4003`, where `close[0]` would simply read this bar.

lowest().src: The series to search, usually `low` or `close`.
lowest().len: How many bars the window covers, this bar included. A whole number of 1 or more.

lowestBars().len: How many bars the window covers, this bar included. A whole number of 1 or more.

median().src: The series whose middle value is taken.
median().len: How many bars the window covers, this bar included. A whole number of 1 or more; with an even count the result is the mean of the two middle values.

percentRank().src: The series whose value on this bar is ranked against its own window.
percentRank().len: How many bars the window covers, this bar included. A whole number of 1 or more.

percentile().src: The series whose values in the window are sorted.
percentile().len: How many bars the window covers, this bar included. A whole number of 1 or more.
percentile().p: The percentile to read, from `0` (the window's lowest value) to `100` (its highest). Between two values the result is interpolated in a straight line, and a `p` outside 0 to 100 gives `none`.

pivotHigh().src: The series to find swing highs in, usually `high`.
pivotHigh().left: How many bars before the pivot must all be lower than it.
pivotHigh().right: How many bars after the pivot must all be lower than it. The value is reported that many bars after the pivot, on the first bar the pivot is known.

pivotLow().src: The series to find swing lows in, usually `low`.
pivotLow().left: How many bars before the pivot must all be higher than it.
pivotLow().right: How many bars after the pivot must all be higher than it. The value is reported that many bars after the pivot, on the first bar the pivot is known.

rising().src: The series to test, such as an average or an oscillator.
rising().len: How many consecutive one bar changes must all be above zero. A whole number of 1 or more; an unchanged bar breaks the run.

sum().src: The series to total over the window. One absent bar in the window makes the total absent.
sum().len: How many bars the window covers, this bar included. A whole number of 1 or more.
sum().arr: An array of numbers, in the form `sum(arr)`, whose elements are all added. An empty array totals `0`, and an absent element makes the total `none`.

sumSkip().src: The series to total. Bars where it is absent are passed over, and a window with no present values totals `0`.
sumSkip().len: How many bars the window covers, this bar included. A whole number of 1 or more.

valueWhen().cond: The event to capture `src` at. A bar where it is absent counts as not true.
valueWhen().src: The value to capture on a bar where `cond` is true, such as `low` at a crossover. It can be of any type.
valueWhen().occurrence: Which true bar to read: `0` is the most recent, `1` the one before it, and so on. A whole number of 0 or more; a fraction or a negative number gives `none` on every bar.
